name: Sikhism
big_question: What did Guru Nanak teach, and how do Sikhs live it out today?

glossary.d: the first Guru, born 1469, who founded the Sikh faith in Punjab
everyone being treated fairly and equally
the tenth Guru, who created the Khalsa and the 5Ks
the Sikh festival celebrating the creation of the Khalsa
a group committed Sikhs join; the word Khalsa means pure
the five artefacts of faith worn by all baptised Sikhs
the free kitchen where Sikhs and all people share food together
the Sikh word for God; it means wondrous enlightener
the belief that refers to the soul; Sikhs also call it the atma
the cycle of death and rebirth that the soul is locked in
cause and effect: what a person does shapes their future
freedom from the cycle of death and rebirth
looking after the world for future generations

lessons.title: Guru Nanak
lessons.big_question: How did Guru Nanak's teachings change the world?
aims: DESCRIBE — who Guru Nanak was and when he lived
DISCUSS — why Guru Nanak taught that all people are equal
EXPLAIN — two lessons that Guru Nanak taught

questions: What does the word equal mean? Give an example from school.
Name one thing you already know about Sikhism.
Why might a new religion need a first teacher?

learn.caption: Guru Nanak's life and his main teachings
rows: Born in Punjab in 1469
Rejected the Sacred Thread Ceremony
One God, responsible for all
All people are equal
Nine more Gurus followed him

source.quote: The Sikh faith started as Guru Nanak realised that people were losing sight of God in their lives because of greed and superstition. He set out a list of new rules.
source.attrib: — Unit 4 lesson slides, on Guru Nanak
source.task: Underline why people were losing sight of God. Then write Guru Nanak's answer in your own words.

stretch.question: Explain two lessons that Guru Nanak taught.

debate.statement: Guru Nanak's teaching about equality is his most important teaching.
agree: He said there is one God for all, so every person must be equal in God's eyes.
He rejected the caste system, so people treated as low-born were finally welcomed in.
disagree: Teaching that there is one God matters more, because equality grows out of that belief.
Sewa, or selfless service, matters more because it changes what Sikhs do every day.
debate.how_to_win: Use one fact about Guru Nanak's life, then say what changed in the world because of it.

quickfire.q: How many sights did the Buddha see?

Where do Buddhists go to worship?

lessons.title: The Five Ks
lessons.big_question: What are the 5Ks? Why are they important today?
aims: DESCRIBE — the 5Ks worn by baptised Sikhs
DISCUSS — why the 5Ks still matter to Sikhs today
EXPLAIN — how the Khalsa began at Vaisakhi in 1699

questions: List as many religious rules or laws as you can.
Why do some religions ask people to wear special items?
Who founded Sikhism, and what did he teach about people?

learn.caption: The 5Ks: five artefacts of faith and what they mean
rows: Kesh - uncut hair, kept in a turban
Kangha - a small wooden comb
Kara - a steel bangle worn on the arm
Kachera - short cotton trousers
Kirpan - a small warrior's sword

source.quote: The 5Ks are items of faith which display and show the wearer's conviction in God and are a constant reminder of their love for Him.
source.task: Highlight the two jobs the 5Ks do. Then pick one K and say what it reminds a Sikh to do.

stretch.question: Why do you think the 5Ks are important to Sikhs?

debate.statement: Wearing the 5Ks is the best way to show you belong to a religion.
agree: The 5Ks are worn all day, so a Sikh is reminded of God every hour, not just in worship.
Guru Gobind Singh gave the 5Ks to the Khalsa, so wearing them links Sikhs back to 1699.
disagree: How you treat other people shows your faith far better than anything you wear.
Sewa, selfless service, actually helps people, while a comb or a bangle only reminds you.
debate.how_to_win: Name one of the 5Ks, say what it symbolises, then judge if a symbol can change behaviour.

quickfire.q: What did Guru Nanak teach about people?
Which K reminds Sikhs to defend the weak?

lessons.title: The Gurdwara
lessons.big_question: Why is the Gurdwara important to Sikhs?
aims: DESCRIBE — what happens inside a gurdwara
DISCUSS — why everyone sits on the floor for langar
EXPLAIN — two ways a gurdwara is important to Sikhs

questions: Why do different religions have their own places of worship?
What might you gain from visiting a gurdwara instead of praying at home?
Name two of the 5Ks and say what each one reminds a Sikh to do.

learn.caption: Inside the gurdwara: worship, holy book and langar
rows: Gurdwara - the Sikh place of worship
Guru Granth Sahib - the Sikh holy book
Langar - free food for everyone
Everyone sits on the floor to eat
Sikhs worship, learn and meet here

source.quote: The Langar provides free food for everyone. It doesn't matter what religion you are - everyone is welcome. This food is offered free of charge.
source.attrib: — Unit 4 lesson slides, on the langar
source.task: Underline who is welcome at langar. Then explain why Sikhs all sit on the floor to eat.

stretch.question: Explain two ways a Gurdwara is important to Sikhs.

debate.statement: Sharing free food does more good than praying together.
agree: Langar feeds anyone who is hungry, of any religion, so it helps people in a real way.
Sitting on the floor together shows nobody is above anyone else, and that builds equality.
disagree: Reading the Guru Granth Sahib teaches Sikhs how to live, which shapes everything else.
Worship brings Sikhs closer to God, and that is the main reason a gurdwara exists.
debate.how_to_win: Give one thing that happens in a gurdwara, then say clearly who it helps and how.

quickfire.q: Where do Buddhists go to worship?
What does the Middle Way teach Buddhists?
Which 5K reminds Sikhs to behave well?
Why do Sikhs sit on the floor at langar?

lessons.title: Formative assessment
lessons.big_question: How much of the Sikhism unit can you explain on your own?
aims: DESCRIBE — the key words of Sikhism studied so far
DISCUSS — which topics you still need to revise
EXPLAIN — two ways a gurdwara is important to Sikhs

questions: Who founded Sikhism, and in which year was he born?
Name three of the 5Ks and say what each one means.
What is langar, and who is welcome to eat there?

learn.caption: Topics the formative assessment covers
learn.col2: What I still need to revise
rows: Guru Nanak: his life and teachings
The 10 Gurus and what they did
The Khalsa, Vaisakhi and the 5Ks
Gurdwara, langar and the holy book
Key words: sewa, karma, mukti, atman

source.quote: One way the Gurdwara is important to Sikhs is that they can have meals together and improve their idea of community.
source.task: Copy this point. Then add a develop sentence that begins with This means that.

stretch.question: Explain two ways a Gurdwara is important to Sikhs.

debate.statement: Tests are the best way to find out what you have really learned.
agree: A test shows exactly which key words you can explain without any help from a book.
Sitting a test now means you can fix your mistakes before the summative assessment.
disagree: You can revise hard and still freeze in a test, so it may not show what you know.
Explaining Sikhism out loud to a partner can prove your learning just as well.
debate.how_to_win: Say what a test does well, what it misses, then give your own view with a reason.

quickfire.q: Name one Buddhist teaching about nature.

lessons.title: Belief in the afterlife
lessons.big_question: What do Sikhs believe happens after death?
aims: DESCRIBE — what Sikhs believe about Waheguru and the atma
DISCUSS — how karma affects the way Sikhs live
EXPLAIN — two Sikh teachings about life after death

questions: If you could share a feast with any famous person, who would you pick?
What do you think happens to a person after they die?
What is a gurdwara, and what happens in the langar?

learn.caption: Sikh beliefs about God, the soul and rebirth
rows: Waheguru - the Sikh name for God
Atma - the soul, given to all beings
Samsara - the cycle of death and rebirth
Mukti - freedom from that cycle
Gurmukh good karma, manmukh bad karma

source.quote: Sikhs have many words to describe God. The name most widely used for God by Sikhs is Waheguru, which means wondrous enlightener.
source.task: Underline what Waheguru means. Then write why Sikhs keep God in their minds all day.

stretch.question: Explain two Sikh teachings about life after death.

debate.statement: Believing in rebirth makes people behave better in this life.
agree: If your karma decides your next life, you have a strong reason to act well every day.
Sikhs try to live as gurmukh, full of good karma, so the belief shapes daily choices.
disagree: Many people behave well without believing in rebirth, simply because it is kind.
Someone might do good deeds only to help themselves, which is not really being good.
debate.how_to_win: Use the words karma and mukti, then say whether a belief can really change behaviour.

quickfire.q: What does the Middle Way teach Buddhists?
Which key word means selfless service?
What is the Sikh name for God?

lessons.title: Sikhism and nature
lessons.big_question: What responsibility do Sikhs have to protect the world?
aims: DESCRIBE — what stewardship means for Sikhs
DISCUSS — why Sikhism has no creation story
EXPLAIN — two reasons Sikhs must look after the world

questions: How many problems in the environment can you name?
Whose job is it to look after the planet? Explain your answer.
What is mukti, and what must Sikhs do to reach it?

learn.caption: Sikh teaching on creation and caring for it
rows: Sikhism has no creation story
Nobody was there when creation happened
Stewardship - caring for the future
Harmony with people, animals, nature
Recycling, clean energy, local food

source.quote: What was that time, and what was that moment? What was that day, and what was that date? What was that season, and what was that month, when the Universe was created?
source.attrib: — Unit 4 slides, quoting the Guru Granth Sahib
source.task: Guru Nanak asks four questions here. Explain in your own words why nobody can answer them.

stretch.question: Explain two reasons why Sikhs must look after the world.

debate.statement: Religious people should do more than others to protect the planet.
agree: The Guru Granth Sahib tells Sikhs to think of future generations, so they have a duty.
Sikhs believe Waheguru created everything, so harming nature harms God's own creation.
disagree: The planet belongs to everyone, so the duty to protect it is equal for all people.
Governments and big companies cause most of the damage, so they should do the most.
debate.how_to_win: Use the word stewardship, give one Sikh teaching, then say clearly what you think.

quickfire.q: How many Noble Truths are there?
Name one Buddhist belief about nature.
Give one way Sikhs can help nature.

lessons.title: Summative assessment
lessons.big_question: Can you explain what Sikhs believe and why it matters?
aims: DESCRIBE — the key words of the whole Sikhism unit
DISCUSS — which answers you can improve next time
EXPLAIN — two Sikh beliefs about the afterlife

questions: Write down three key words from this unit and their meanings.
What do Sikhs believe happens to the atma after death?
Why do Sikhs believe they must look after the world?

learn.caption: What the summative assessment covers
rows: Match 10 key words to their meanings
Two Sikh beliefs about the afterlife
Two Sikh beliefs about nature
Outline two of the 5Ks
A Point and a Develop in every answer

source.quote: Firstly, human beings are stewards of God's creation. This means that we are meant to look after Waheguru's creation for the future.
source.task: Circle the point and the explanation. Then write your own pair about Sikh belief in mukti.

stretch.question: Explain two Sikh beliefs about nature.

debate.statement: Sikhism says more about how to live than about what happens after death.
agree: Sewa, langar and the 5Ks are all about daily actions that any Sikh can see and do.
Sikhs are told to live as gurmukh now, because good karma is built in this life.
disagree: Everything Sikhs do is aimed at mukti, so the afterlife is the real reason behind it.
Beliefs about samsara and karma are what explain why daily actions matter at all.
debate.how_to_win: Use one belief about life now and one about the afterlife, then say which is bigger.

quickfire.q: Name the Buddhist place of worship.
Do Sikhs have a creation story?
